segments.text: This is what a single sine wave sounds like. Yeah, just one perfect smooth tone.
It can be played faster, slower, louder and quieter, but something cool happens when we add a bunch of them together.
If we align the sine waves just right, we get a sawtooth wave.
Neat. Or if you combine only half of them, we end up with a square wave.
Or if you combine them in this way, you get a triangle wave.
Turns out, you could create literally any waveform just by combining sine waves.
We'll use this and more techniques to make the sound effects and music in this experiment.
But a similar idea can be used in two dimensions. If we control how high up or down this dot is by fixing it to a sine wave, then we control how far left and right it is by fixing it to a
copy of the sine wave, then as long as we offset one side by a quarter turn, the dot goes in a perfect circle.
Just like before, we can add in a higher frequency sign, and in this case it makes like a cloud or some loops.
